\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Daily return of the sign strategy (\% of the premium, an excess return), \rhebNDays{} post-warmup days. $r^{m}_t$: S\&P~500 close-to-close price return minus the three-month Treasury bill; $r^{30}_t$: the index's 15:30--16:00 ET return. $\beta$, $\gamma$: slopes on $r^{m}_t$ and its square \citep{TreynorMazuy1966}; worst decile: mean return on the tenth of the days with the lowest $r^{m}_t$ (stars and $t$: its difference from the other days). $t$-statistics in parentheses (Newey--West, $S = \rheHACS$, fixed-$b$). $^{*}$, $^{**}$ and $^{***}$ denote significance at the 10\%, 5\% and 1\% levels. Maximum $\SR$: the in-sample tangency portfolio of the market ($\SR_m = \rhebSRm$) and the strategy, with the block-bootstrap $p$-value of its gain in brackets; GRS $p$: the test of $\alpha = 0$ \citep{GibbonsRossShanken1989}; risk share: the strategy's share of the tangency portfolio's volatility. Mean--variance and inverse volatility: weights from earlier days only, on the \rhebNRt{} days from \rhebRtFirst{} (market $\rhebSRmRt$; without the best days of Table~\ref{tab:rh_econ_bestdays}, $\rhebSRmEx$ in sample and $\rhebSRmExRt$ in real time); no short positions, neither leg above \rhebCap\% of the volatility; inverse volatility over the trailing \rhebNTrail{} days; in brackets, the $p$-value of the \citet{LedoitWolf2008} test of its gain over the market. Every $\SR$ here is the paper's: $\sqrt{q}$ times the mean over the standard deviation of the daily returns, $q$ the days per calendar year of the sample (\rheAnnDays{} on the \rhebNDays{} days, \rhebQRt{} on the \rhebNRt{} real-time days).
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
